bull_bear.body: QIP of INR1,000cr planned for organic growth (capacity) and inorganic M&A (tech-enabled auto components); no promoter participation; debt repayment (NCDs: INR500cr in 18m, INR500cr in 24m) on schedule; dividend: Final INR5/share recommended (total INR10/share FY26)
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical disruption to exports (Middle East/Europe); commodity volatility (aluminum); integration delays in Antolin synergies; execution risk in capex ramp-up; regulatory delays in EV adoption
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, aggressive, and execution-focused; strong emphasis on technology leadership, ESG credibility, and disciplined M&A; transparent on margin roadmaps but cautious on disclosure due to competition
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Antolin’s headliner dominance (75% market share) is not a ceiling — continuous model changes drive new variants, ensuring organic growth; 60% powertrain-agnostic mix is a strategic outcome of legacy business resilience, not just EV exposure; ESG certifications (CDP B, Dun & Bradstreet 2/5, EcoVadis Bronze) are material differentiators for OEM selection
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: Legacy (Pistons/Rings): 65% of revenue, +10-11% YoY growth across PVs, CVs, 2W, tractors; Antolin (Interiors/Lighting): Acquired Jan 2026, contributing to revenue, margins improving from ~9-10% to target ~20%; Takahata/TGPEL (Precision Molding): TAM ~INR3,500cr, targeting 20-30% share; EV Motors & Controllers: EBITDA positive, Coimbatore plant operational, serving 2W/4W EVs with hairpin winding tech
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

latest_quarter.body: Commodity (aluminum +40% YoY) fully pass-through to OEMs with 1-quarter lag; labor shortages mitigated by premium wages; energy stable; margin uplift expected via in-sourcing, supply chain optimization, and synergy realization across subsidiaries
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: revenue growth: 'Healthy pipeline' with multi-year programs (2029-30); margin: Subsidiaries to approach stand-alone margin (~21-22%) within <3 years; order inflow: 'Exciting' new programs across interiors, plastics, EV motors; capex/commissioning: ~INR200cr/year over next 2-3 years; Neemrana (Takahata Phase 3), Noida (TGPEL), Pithampur (SPL Phase 3) under expansion
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Expansion into non-automotive (medical/industrial) precision parts; export recovery in LATAM/Middle East; inorganic growth via M&A in tech-enabled auto components (e.g., sensors, ADAS, high-voltage systems); synergy-driven cross-selling between Antolin and plastics divisions
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: SPR Auto Technologies delivered record FY26 revenue (INR4,571cr, +25% YoY) and EBITDA (INR989cr, +18% YoY) driven by strategic acquisitions (Antolin, Karna) and capacity expansions, with 60% of business now powertrain-agnostic — this structural shift reduces ICE dependency and positions the company as a diversified mobility tech platform with margin expansion potential across subsidiaries.

drhp.business: SPR Auto Technologies Limited (formerly Shriram Pistons & Rings Limited) manufactures pistons, piston rings and engine valves for automotive, off-highway vehicles, farm equipment, genset engines and compressors. Following the FY2025-26 acquisition of Grupo Antolin's Indian operations, it has expanded beyond its core powertrain components into automotive interior solutions and interior lighting. The company supplies OEMs, aftermarket and non-automotive applications in India and export markets.
